findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves, in plain words. This part works.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: A newcomer who comes to Athena's site lands on a long study of a different tool, firstmate. The second and third lede paragraphs explain why, but most of the page is about firstmate's internals, not about Athena.

The one section that could show Athena's main promise (models, verdict and cost traced to a request) is the first section after the nav, and it shows an error. A newcomer sees the core claim go unproven, which hurts trust.
findings.source: Check it on a real job — "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link sits in the header next to the next-step link, but it is meant for the project owner. A newcomer may not know whether it is meant for them.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: a clone command, prerequisites, a setup script and a first command, with a note that it acts on the current repository and waits for Enter. A newcomer knows what to do next, and the header links straight here.
findings.source: Next steps — "Before installing, check that you have these prerequisites: git 2.40 or later; a C linker (cc)...; curl...; Claude Code, or npm to install it." and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Several terms the page uses are admitted to be undefined. That is honest, but the firstmate explanation leaves gaps that a newcomer cannot fill.
findings.source: Glossary — "captain call: The firstmate source does not define a captain call." (also durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake)

findings.text: Even the core track (the default view) uses exit codes, lock contention and pending-close records within the first screens. That goes deeper than a newcomer needs just to see what Athena can do.
findings.source: Start here — "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: This points to a repository folder without a link and without saying which repository it is in. It is internal detail that does a newcomer no good.
findings.source: About this page — "is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
